record.paper_title: Progresses on Some Open Problems Related to Infinitely Many Symmetries
record.original_question: Given a particular solution u0(x,t) of a system, can the action of infinitely many symmetries introduce an infinite sequence of arbitrary constants into that specific solution, extending the familiar use of spatial and temporal translation symmetries to introduce constants such as x0 and t0?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let a nonlinear evolution system for an unknown function u(x,t) admit an infinite hierarchy of (generalized) Lie–point symmetries {K_n}_{n=0}^∞, in the sense that each K_n is a characteristic of a one-parameter group of transformations leaving the system formally invariant. Recall the elementary fact that the translation symmetries K_∂x = u_x and K_∂t = u_t allow one to introduce two arbitrary constants x_0 and t_0 into any particular solution u_0(x,t) by the replacement u_0(x,t) ↦ u_0(x − x_0, t − t_0).

Question: Given any particular solution u_0(x,t) of such a system, does the action of the full infinite hierarchy {K_n} on u_0 produce an infinite sequence of independent arbitrary constants {c_n}_{n=0}^∞ in that solution, in such a way that each new constant arises from an additional symmetry beyond the spatial and temporal translations and the resulting family of deformed solutions remains a solution of the original system?

Equivalently, can every solution of an integrable system carrying infinitely many commuting symmetries be embedded into an infinite-parameter family of solutions obtained by exponentiating those symmetries, with the parameters c_n playing the role of generalized "translation" constants associated with intrinsic wave parameters (positions, widths, periods, etc.) of the constituent waves?
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture that all known infinite symmetries are linear combinations of finite wave-parameter translation symmetries (and thus introduce infinitely many arbitrary constants of translation type into particular multi-wave solutions) has been empirically verified for the KdV, Burgers, modified KdV, Sawada–Kotera, nonlinear Schrödinger, Boussinesq, Sharma–Tasso–Olver and sine-Gordon equations, but it remains an open conjecture in general for arbitrary integrable systems.

status_evidence.title: Progresses on some open problems related to infinitely many symmetries
status_evidence.snippet: Investigation of five open problems concerning infinitely many symmetries, including the role of arbitrary constants in particular solutions and a conjecture that infinite symmetries are linear combinations of wave-parameter translation symmetries.
status_evidence.claim: The arbitrary-constants question is identified as an open problem, with verification only on a finite list of integrable equations.

status_evidence.title: From one to infinity: symmetries of integrable systems
status_evidence.snippet: Studies how hierarchies of symmetries in integrable systems generate families of solutions parametrized by additional constants.
status_evidence.claim: Related results support partial progress for specific integrable hierarchies.
